articles.title: Gogoro Secures $61.8 Million In New Equity Investments
articles.snippet:
Gogoro announced approximately $61.8 million in new equity investments from entities controlled by director Chung-Yao Yin and additional strategic investors, providing the electric mobility company with additional capital to support its balance sheet and long-term growth plans.
The post Gogoro Secures $61.8 Million In New Equity Investments appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Gogoro Secures $61.8 Million In New Equity Investments
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Gogoro Secures $61.8 Million In New Equity Investments
Gogoro announced approximately $61.8 million in new equity investments from entities controlled by director Chung-Yao Yin and additional strategic investors, providing the electric mobility company with additional capital to support its balance sheet and long-term growth plans.
The company plans to issue approximately 24.94 million ordinary shares at a purchase price of $2.48 per share.
Participants in the financing include Gold Sino Asset Limited and Peng-Lin Investment Limited, both controlled by Yin, as well as Ruen Hua Dyeing & Weaving and Yi Tai Investment.
Following completion of the transaction, Gold Sino is expected to beneficially own approximately 45% of Gogoro’s outstanding ordinary shares.
Peng-Lin is expected to hold approximately 8.8%, while Ruen Hua and its affiliates are expected to beneficially own approximately 21.9% of the company.
The financing represents a second round of new equity investments involving entities controlled by Yin and other strategic investors, further increasing their financial commitment to Gogoro.
Gogoro said the new capital will strengthen its balance sheet and provide additional resources to support continued business development and the execution of its long-term growth strategy.
The transaction has been reviewed and approved by Gogoro’s Audit Committee and Board of Directors.
Closing remains subject to customary conditions, including required Nasdaq clearance.
Gogoro expects the investment to be funded on or before October 13, 2026.
The additional equity comes as Gogoro continues operating and developing its battery-swapping ecosystem for electric two-wheel transportation.
The company’s network supports nearly 700,000 riders and includes more than 2,700 GoStation battery-swapping locations.
Gogoro’s platform is designed to provide riders with rapid access to charged batteries while supporting a broader electric mobility ecosystem spanning vehicles, battery technology, software, and energy infrastructure.
The $61.8 million financing gives the company additional financial flexibility as it continues investing in its network, technology, and broader business strategy.

articles.title: Braavo Capital Commits Over $60 Million To Expand UA Cohort Financing For Mobile Apps
articles.snippet:
Braavo Capital has committed more than $60 million to user acquisition cohort financing facilities in 2026, expanding its non-dilutive funding platform for mobile app and game companies.
The post Braavo Capital Commits Over $60 Million To Expand UA Cohort Financing For Mobile Apps appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Braavo Capital Commits Over $60 Million To Expand UA Cohort Financing For Mobile Apps
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Braavo Capital Commits Over $60 Million To Expand UA Cohort Financing For Mobile Apps
Braavo Capital has committed more than $60 million to user acquisition cohort financing facilities in 2026, expanding its non-dilutive funding platform for mobile app and game companies.
The New York-based company provides committed capital that customers can draw as they spend on user acquisition. Rather than structuring advances against an entire company’s revenue or balance sheet, Braavo scopes each advance to a specific user acquisition cohort and is repaid from the revenue generated by that cohort.
Braavo said the model allows mobile companies to fund advertising and customer acquisition without using equity capital for those expenses. The financing is designed around the economics of individual cohorts, including expected return on advertising spend, revenue generation, and the way customer acquisition performance develops over time.
Recent commitments include $15 million for children’s tutoring app Buddy.ai and $15 million for AI-powered skincare app Lovi.
Buddy.ai has worked with Braavo since 2019 and previously completed six user acquisition financing transactions with the company. The latest facility provides the business with committed capacity that can be used to plan a longer period of customer acquisition spending while preserving equity for product development and hiring.
Lovi closed its facility in June and has since tripled its advertising spend. Braavo said its underwriting process combines data integrations with analysis of subscription economics to develop financing structures tailored to individual customers.
The company positions its experience underwriting mobile app businesses as a key part of its ability to assess how user acquisition can scale and how return-on-ad-spend curves may change as spending increases.
Founded in New York City in 2015, Braavo Capital focuses on non-dilutive financing for mobile application companies. The company said it has tracked more than $5 billion in app earnings across 10,000 applications and more than $1.5 billion in user acquisition spending.
The more than $60 million committed this year adds to Braavo’s broader effort to give app developers and publishers an alternative source of growth capital specifically tied to customer acquisition performance.
KEY QUOTES:
“The mechanics of cohort financing aren’t complicated. The harder part is understanding how a company can scale user acquisition, how its ROAS curves will evolve over time, and how much flexibility you can responsibly build into a facility. Our experience lets us structure around a customer’s actual economics rather than starting with a predetermined template.”
Mark Loranger, CEO Of Braavo Capital
“Even when we considered alternatives for a larger cohort financing facility, Braavo still came out on top. Seven years in, I know how they work and even what to expect if something doesn’t go to plan.”
“A committed facility means we can scale user acquisition without tying up equity to do it. We know the terms, we know how the cohorts have to perform, and we can plan a year of user acquisition instead of a quarter. Equity goes into the product and the team.”
Ivan Crewkov, CEO Of Buddy.ai

articles.title: Certified Origins Secures $60 Million Revolver From CIT Northbridge
articles.snippet:
Certified Origins has secured a $60 million asset-based revolving credit facility from CIT Northbridge to support the food company's continued growth and investment in North America.
The post Certified Origins Secures $60 Million Revolver From CIT Northbridge appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Certified Origins Secures $60 Million Revolver From CIT Northbridge
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
Certified Origins Secures $60 Million Revolver From CIT Northbridge
Certified Origins has secured a $60 million asset-based revolving credit facility from CIT Northbridge to support the food company’s continued growth and investment in North America.
CIT Northbridge served as sole lender on the transaction, while Arch & Beam advised Certified Origins.
Headquartered in Tuscany, Italy, Certified Origins operates U.S. manufacturing facilities in Newport News, Virginia, and Fresno, California.
The company specializes in private-label and co-packing food products, including extra virgin olive oil, tomato sauce, tree nuts and nut butters.
Certified Origins works with growers and producers throughout the Mediterranean region and provides traceable food products to retail and industrial customers in North America and other international markets.
The financing gives Certified Origins additional liquidity as it continues integrating its businesses and investing in its North American operations.
CIT Northbridge provides asset-based revolving and term financing ranging from $15 million to $150 million for middle-market companies across a range of industries.
KEY QUOTES:
“CIT Northbridge’s understanding of our business and ability to deliver a tailored financing solution made them an ideal banking partner as we continue integrating our businesses and investing in the growth of our company in North America.”
Rod Hogan, CFO of Certified Origins
“Certified Origins has built a strong reputation as a trusted provider of high-quality products. We are pleased to extend this recent financing, which provides Certified Origins with additional flexibility to pursue its strategic growth objectives.”
Neal Legan, Business Leader at CIT Northbridge

articles.title: Sibelco Signs Deal For Up To $56 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance High-Purity Quartz Processing In North Carolina
articles.snippet:
Sibelco, a global materials solutions company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $56 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. The funding would support research, development, and commercialization activities involving next-generation high-purity quartz processing technologies for semiconductor manufacturing in the United States.
The post Sibelco Signs Deal For Up To $56 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance High-Purity Quartz Processing In North Carolina appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Sibelco Signs Deal For Up To $56 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance High-Purity Quartz Processing In North Carolina
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Sibelco Signs Deal For Up To $56 Million In CHIPS Act Funding To Advance High-Purity Quartz Processing In North Carolina
Sibelco, a global materials solutions company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $56 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. The funding would support research, development, and commercialization activities involving next-generation high-purity quartz processing technologies for semiconductor manufacturing in the United States.
The agreement, announced October 22, 2026, through Sibelco North America, could strengthen domestic capabilities to produce semiconductor-grade, high-purity quartz, a material used in critical components throughout the chip manufacturing process.
The proposed funding would support Sibelco’s U.S. research and development operations, building on the company’s longstanding presence and technical expertise in Spruce Pine, North Carolina.
High-purity quartz is an important raw material used to manufacture specialized quartz components for semiconductor fabrication. These components must meet demanding purity and performance requirements because contamination during manufacturing can affect semiconductor production quality and efficiency.
As semiconductor manufacturers expand domestic production capacity, access to reliable supplies of high-purity materials has become increasingly important for supply chain resilience and advanced technology development.
Sibelco’s proposed research program would focus on four areas intended to advance processing efficiency, material quality, and the scalability of semiconductor-grade quartz production.
The first involves next-generation leaching technologies, which are used to remove impurities from quartz materials. Improvements in these processes could support the production of higher-purity materials suitable for increasingly sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing applications.
The second area involves advanced hot chlorination technologies, which provide additional processing capabilities for reducing impurities and improving material purity.
A third component focuses on high-purity quartz product engineering, with research intended to enhance material properties and develop products that meet evolving requirements across semiconductor manufacturing processes.
The fourth area involves establishing a technology piloting and demonstration facility to test, validate, and scale new quartz processing methods and products.
This facility would provide infrastructure for evaluating emerging technologies before broader industrial deployment, helping bridge the gap between laboratory research and commercial-scale production.
Together, these activities are intended to support the domestic development of advanced processing technologies and strengthen the availability of critical materials within the U.S. semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.
The proposed award aligns with broader federal efforts under the CHIPS and Science Act to expand semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, strengthen supply chains, and support research and technological innovation in the United States.
The initiative also highlights the importance of North Carolina’s established high-purity quartz industry to advanced manufacturing and national technology infrastructure.

articles.title: Gaius Capital Closes Debut Private Equity Funds At €56 Million
articles.snippet:
Gaius Capital reached the final close of its debut private equity funds with €56 million in total capital raised.
The post Gaius Capital Closes Debut Private Equity Funds At €56 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Gaius Capital Closes Debut Private Equity Funds At €56 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Gaius Capital Closes Debut Private Equity Funds At €56 Million
Gaius Capital reached the final close of its debut private equity funds with €56 million in total capital raised.
The total includes €50 million for Gaius Nachfolgekapital I, which closed oversubscribed at its hard cap, along with an additional €6 million raised through a co-investment vehicle.
The final close came approximately four months after Gaius Capital completed a €40 million first close in June 2026.
More than 90% of commitments came from institutional investors across Germany, France, the Benelux region, the United States, and the United Kingdom.
Gaius Capital is an independent private equity firm focused on succession solutions in the DACH Mittelstand.
The firm targets scalable buy-and-build strategies across the micro- and small-cap segments and partners with business owners on succession transitions.
Gaius Capital said its approach is designed to preserve and extend the value created by entrepreneurs while providing a platform for continued growth.
Since its first close, the firm has continued deploying capital and building new succession platforms.
In September 2026, Gaius Capital launched Alpiora Group in Switzerland as its second succession platform.
That followed the firm’s first platform, which is focused on insurance brokers in Germany.
With the fundraising process completed, Gaius Capital plans to build additional succession platforms across resilient-growth service industries in the DACH region.
The firm is also continuing to expand its investment team as it develops additional private equity platforms.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are very grateful to our investors for their trust and support throughout this journey. Reaching the final close at our hard cap, with significant demand from an experienced institutional investor base, is a strong endorsement of our strategy and the opportunity we see in Mittelstand succession. With the fundraise successfully completed, our focus is now on deploying capital thoughtfully and building lasting partnerships with entrepreneurs across the DACH region.”
Jan Mickel, Founding Partner of Gaius Capital
